body: Label `merge-ready`: the review at f5e3155 found no blocker and the PR is MERGEABLE with main. The PR is still a draft. Its author flags it ready, and a maintainer merges by hand.

Route note: merged at 09:36Z as `d210c7c0d` by another session, on the review at `f5e3155dc`. The coordinator's own safety-floor review of the same head is still running: the failing-first check of the fig8 pins with the old `SIDE_EPS`, and the untested edge route in `pass_link`. Its result follows here as a tip check of `d210c7c0d`. If it finds a fault, a P1 follow-up is filed at once.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f5e3155dc2190a26f5fdeab5d80dc9b349bb9de4 -->
**Post-merge tip check (the PR merged as `d210c7c0d` during this review).** No P1 found. Each pin fails without the fix. The edge route cannot skip the proof, but no test reaches it (follow-up 1 below).

The verdict for the head `f5e3155dc` is clean. It has two non-blocking follow-ups. No label is set, because the PR is merged.

## What looks good
- The cause is in the right place. `sides` classifies only the area's own boundary. A change of class changes the order and the level of a piece. It does not move a cutter-centre point. Thus a misread of the side cannot put the tool off the certified area.
- The unit pin `the_side_tolerance_keeps_a_real_short_wall_and_drops_a_flat_sliver` checks both sides of the tolerance: 50 um stays a wall, and 5 um reads as the start side.
- The edge route (`ring_links::link`) proves each chord of the route with `chord_proof`. The proof checks the certified area, a crossing of `passes` and `st.level`, and the air or cut-column samples. It checks the whole walk against the stay-down limit before it pushes a feed. A failed route keeps the reason of the straight chord. I found no path that skips the proof, leaves the area, or crosses the part.
- The `dead_end_ramp` block in `ladder_links::pass_link` is not changed (#3748 owns it). The `Link::Clearance` arm from #3837/#3822 is intact (`ladder_links.rs` lines 181-186 on the head).
- The clamp Inside lifts go from 3 to 4. Each lift is named. The decision file records the tangent meeting of the clamp keep-out and the part ring, and its sensitivity to the tolerance (2 lifts at 2 um, 4 lifts from 3 to 10 um). I accept this.

## Results (local)
Trial merge of the head with `origin/main` `f2aa981b5`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6) | `wall 35.3 min, 173 step(s), 0 failed, 0 stalled`; `motion suites: pass_start_levels` ok, `app suites: offset_pass_start` ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Merged tip `d210c7c0d` (with #3858 and #3458, which landed between): `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start --test flute_reach -- --include-ignored`. `offset_pass_start` 16 passed. `flute_reach` 4 passed.

## Red first
I set only `SIDE_EPS` back to `1e-3` in the review tree and kept the edge route. Then I ran the pins in release:
- `fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material`: FAILED, `Outside: a plunge into material (4 named)` (at (46.482, 123.140), Z 12.000).
- `lifts::fig8_outside_pass_links_keep_off_the_part_and_enter_on_cut_floor`: FAILED, `#3825: a pass link lifts over the part`.
- `lifts::fig8_start_sides_lift_only_with_a_named_reason`: FAILED, `Inside: 6 lifts inside a level (#3824: at most 0)`.
- `flute_reach::a_ten_mm_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_rapid_findings`: FAILED, `flute 10: 9 rapid finding(s)`, bound 3.

These results agree with the "before" readings of the author. They also show that the edge route alone changes nothing on fig8.

## Heavy lanes
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main` reaches 101 steps: `motion heavy` and `app heavy`, every target. This review ran the targeted steps in release:
- `motion heavy: pass_start_levels`: ok (497 s).
- `app heavy: flute_reach`: ok (605 s).
- `app heavy: offset_pass_start`: ok (65 s); also green on the merged tip (above).

The other reached steps were not run here. They run at the cut.

## Follow-ups (not blocking, since the PR is merged)
1. **The edge route has no pin.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs` lines 141-155 (the `Err(why)` arm of `link`) is safety-path code that no test reaches. Add a pin in `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels/` that takes this branch, for example two pass starts on one loop of the area with a cut between them on the straight chord. The pin must assert the posted walk, `st.level` and no crossing. If no pin can reach the branch, remove the branch. I recommend a `source:agent` issue for this.
2. **`SIDE_EPS` is a literal.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:41` sets `1e-2`, and the comment ties it to `ARC_TOL_UNITS`, but that constant is `pub(crate)` in `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs:40`. Export the flattening error in mm (for example `geo2d::ARC_TOL`). Then derive `SIDE_EPS` from it, so a change of the flats moves the side tolerance too. The user's chord tolerance does not feed `Region::offset`, so the geometry constant is the right source.
3. **The margin is tight in the worst case.** "Twice the flats" does not count the flattening of the `offset(SIDE_EPS)` grow itself. At a sharp convex corner of the start side, the 10 um round join with a 5 um arc tolerance can stand only about 5 um out. The 10 um margin can then fall to about 0 against two 5 um flats. This does not occur on fig8, and a misread does not move the tool (see above). Consider `3 * ARC_TOL`, or a finer arc tolerance for that one grow, when you do item 2.

## Notes
- A real wall stretch within 10 um of the start side means a band narrower than 10 um. A cut cannot see that difference. The tolerance is absolute, so small parts do not change the result.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
